advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a CODE-path (rs.materialize) test with a pre-existing adjacent donor entry where the target/donor tree holds a symlink or gitlink, asserting the donor branch fails closed and the resulting entry still byte-matches its committed SHA.
evidence: Diff adds new branch: `if not materialize_via_donor(root_dir, sha, build, store=store, entry_prefix="", subdir=""): _materialize_tree(root_dir, sha, build)`

Contract in the added comment: 'trees holding symlinks or gitlinks fall back to the full build' and the helper 'fails CLOSED (returns False) on any doubt — donor mismatch, symlink/gitlink in the tree'

The new test test_adjacent_code_shas_reuse_unchanged_blobs (tests/unit/test_repo_snapshot.py:466-481) only commits plain 20KB text blobs, so the donor branch always SUCCEEDS; the False->full-build fallback for CODE entries is never taken.

Existing test_submodule_gitlink_omitted_and_recorded (tests/unit/test_repo_snapshot.py:113-137) materializes a SINGLE SHA with no prior neighbouring entry, so it exercises the full-build path with no donor present — it cannot regress the new donor-present fallback.
advisory.finding: The new CODE donor branch's fail-closed fallback is untested: no test drives rs.materialize() across adjacent SHAs where a hardlink donor entry exists but the tree holds a symlink or gitlink, so the contract's claim that such trees 'fall back to the full build' and still byte-match their SHA is not exercised on the code (bare <sha>) path.
scenarios: A code SHA whose tree gains a symlink or gitlink while an adjacent code entry already exists as a donor candidate: a regression that let the donor path (mis)handle the symlink/gitlink instead of falling back would produce an unfaithful entry and go undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that materializes an initial code SHA (creating a donor), then commits a SHA that adds a symlink (or gitlink), materializes it, and asserts (a) the entry byte-matches git ls-tree at that SHA and (b) the fallback ran (e.g. the changed/symlink path is not hardlink-shared with the donor).
